object.medium: Single-board microcomputer: printed circuit board with integrated circuits
materials: wood (base, as sold by some dealers)
object.description: The Apple Computer 1 is an 8-bit personal computer designed by Steve Wozniak and sold from July 1976 by the newly founded Apple Computer Company, with Steve Jobs handling the business side. Unlike most hobbyist computers of its day it was delivered as a fully assembled and tested circuit board, built around a MOS 6502 processor; the buyer still had to add a power supply, keyboard, cassette recorder and television. The board shown here is an artist's reconstruction of a complete Apple I set-up, including the optional wooden case and Apple-1 Operation Manual.
facts: Sold for $666.66; Wozniak chose the price because he liked repeating digits.
Only about 175 to 200 boards were made before the Apple II replaced it; production ended on 30 September 1977.
Ran a MOS 6502 processor at 1 MHz with 4 KB of RAM (expandable to 8 KB) and displayed 40 x 24 characters on a television.
